blocks.text: **Lectures 9–11.** Question 2 gives you a PDF or a CDF (or names one: uniform, exponential, normal) and asks for $c$, the CDF, and probabilities. It’s all about how the **PDF**, the **CDF** and **probability** connect.
Topic 1: PDF ↔ CDF ↔ probability
$X$ can be any number in a range: a time, a voltage, a length. Its **PDF** $f_X(x)$ is a curve. The curve’s height is **not** a probability. The **area under it** is.
**Compared with Question 1:** a PMF gives a chance at each point, and you **add** them. A PDF gives a height, and you take **area** (integrate).
**The 5 formulas.** $f_X$ = the PDF (height of the curve), $F_X$ = the CDF (area so far), $a$ and $b$ = the ends of the range you’re asked about.
**1. Total area = 1.** This is how you find an unknown $c$:
**2. CDF = the area from the far left up to $x$.** It starts at $0$ on the left and ends at $1$ on the right. ($t$ is just a placeholder letter, so it doesn’t clash with the $x$ at the top.)
**3. PDF = the slope of the CDF.** Going back is a derivative:
**4. Probability = area between = a difference of $F$’s.** Every probability turns into $F$’s:
**5. One exact value has chance 0.** So $<$ and $\le$ give the same answer.

**See it:** $f(x)=\tfrac x2$ on $[0,2]$. The shaded area left of $x$ is exactly the height of the CDF at $x$.

```graph
title "Drag $x$: the shaded area under the PDF is the CDF $F(x)$"
x -0.3 2.4 label="$x$" height=250
y 0 1.15 label=""
slider X 0 2 1 step=0.05 label="$x$" animate
region "(x>0)*(x<X)*(y>0)*(y<x/2)"
curve "x/2" from=0 to=2 color=1 label="PDF $f(x)=x/2$"
curve "x^2/4" from=0 to=2 color=2 label="CDF $F(x)=x^2/4$"
segment "X" "0" "X" "X^2/4" color=0 dash
point "X" "X^2/4" color=2
```
**What to do, by what you have and what you want:**

rows: integrate from the left end up to $x$

blocks.text: **Piecewise PDF** (a triangle, or a formula that changes at some $x$): split at every corner. On each piece, $F_X(x)$ = all the area of the earlier pieces + the area of this piece up to $x$. Before the range $F_X=0$; after it $F_X=1$.

**Integrals you’ll need**

$$
\int x^n\,dx=\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\qquad\qquad \int e^{-\lambda x}\,dx=-\frac1\lambda\,e^{-\lambda x}
$$

By parts, for $x\,e^{-x}$ (take $u=x$, $dv=e^{-x}dx$):

$$
\int x\,e^{-x}\,dx=-(x+1)\,e^{-x}
$$

Shortcut (not from the lectures, good for checking):

$$
\int_0^{\infty}x^n\,e^{-\lambda x}\,dx=\frac{n!}{\lambda^{n+1}}
$$
**Examples: one for each kind of question.**

blocks.title: Example 1 · Find $c$, then the CDF and a probability · Practice 02 Q1
blocks.prompt: $f_X(x)=c(1-x^4)$ for $-1\le x\le1$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find $c$, the CDF, and $P(|X|<\tfrac12)$.

steps.explanation: **Find $c$:** integrate over the range, set it to $1$.
**Accumulate:** the area from $-1$ up to $x$. It’s $0$ before $-1$ and $1$ after $1$.
**Rewrite:** $|X|<\tfrac12$ means $-\tfrac12<X<\tfrac12$. The PDF is symmetric, so double the area on $[0,\tfrac12]$.

blocks.title: Example 2 · Find $c$ fast: the triangle shortcut · Tutorial 4 Q2
blocks.prompt: $X$ has a triangle PDF: $0$ at $x=1$, peak height $c$ at $x=3$, back to $0$ at $x=5$. Find $c$ and write $f_X$.

steps.explanation: **Spot:** the PDF is a triangle, so skip the integral. Area of a triangle $=\tfrac12\cdot$ base $\cdot$ height.
**Read off:** the base runs from $1$ to $5$.
Each side is a straight line: it climbs $\tfrac12$ over $2$ units, so the slope is $\tfrac14$.

blocks.title: Example 3 · PDF → CDF, piece by piece · Tutorial 4 Q2
blocks.prompt: Same triangle: $f_X(x)=\tfrac{x-1}{4}$ on $[1,3]$ and $\tfrac{5-x}{4}$ on $[3,5]$. Find the CDF and $P(2<X<3.5)$.

steps.explanation: **Spot:** have $f$, want $F$ → integrate. The PDF changes at $x=3$, so do two pieces.
**Accumulate**, left piece: the area from $1$ up to $x$.
**Accumulate**, right piece: everything ($1$) minus the small triangle still to come on the right.
**Check:** both pieces give $\tfrac12$ at $x=3$ (the peak splits the area in half).
**Rewrite** $P(2<X<3.5)=F(3.5)-F(2)$, then **plug in**: $3.5$ is on the right piece, $2$ on the left.

blocks.title: Example 4 · CDF → probabilities and the PDF · Lecture 9
blocks.prompt: $F_X(x)=\tfrac x4$ for $0\le x\le4$ ($0$ before, $1$ after). Find (a) $P(X\le-1)$, (b) $P(X\le1)$, (c) $P(2<X\le3)$, (d) $P(X>1)$, (e) $P(X=1)$, (f) the PDF.

blocks.title: Example 5 · Working backwards: find the cut-off $b$
blocks.prompt: $f_X(x)=\tfrac x2$ on $[0,2]$ (the PDF in the graph above). (a) Find $b$ with $P(X\le b)=\tfrac12$. (b) Find the value that only the top $10\%$ are above.

steps.explanation: **Spot:** given a probability, want the cut-off → get $F$, set it equal, solve.
(b) Top $10\%$ above $b$ means $90\%$ below it: set $F_X(b)=0.9$.

blocks.text: Topic 2: Uniform and exponential
When the question **names** the PDF, it’s ready-made: no $c$ to find. Just learn these two and use Topic 1’s rules on them.
**Uniform$(a,b)$:** “uniformly at random between $a$ and $b$”. $a$ = the left end, $b$ = the right end. The PDF is flat:
Flat means every probability is just a **length ratio**:

blocks.latex: P(X\text{ lands in a piece})=\frac{\text{length of the piece}}{b-a}

blocks.text: **Exponential$(\lambda)$:** a lifetime or a waiting time. $\lambda$ = the rate (per hour, per minute), $x\ge0$ = the time. Given the **mean** instead? Then $\lambda=\dfrac1{\text{mean}}$.

blocks.latex: f_X(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x},\qquad F_X(x)=1-e^{-\lambda x},\qquad x\ge0

blocks.text: You’ll use the **tail** (chance it lasts longer than $x$) more than the CDF. A “between” is a difference of two tails:
**Memoryless:** “it has already lasted $s$; chance it lasts $t$ more?” The time already waited doesn’t matter: an old part is as good as new. $s$ = time already lasted, $t$ = the extra time.
**Examples.**

blocks.title: Example 6 · Uniform: length ÷ length · Tutorial 2 Q5
blocks.prompt: A bus comes at a uniform random time between 1:00 and 1:30. What’s the chance you wait at least 10 minutes (arriving at 1:00)?

steps.explanation: **Rewrite:** waiting at least 10 means the bus comes in $[10,30]$, a piece of length $20$.

blocks.title: Example 7 · Uniform, with an event to rewrite · Tutorial 3 Q1
blocks.prompt: Pick $X$ uniformly in $(0,\tfrac\pi2)$. What’s the chance $\sin X>\cos X$?

steps.explanation: **Rewrite** the event as a range of $X$: $\sin x$ passes $\cos x$ at $x=\tfrac\pi4$.

blocks.title: Example 8 · Exponential: tail and between
blocks.prompt: A part’s lifetime is exponential with a mean of 500 hours. Find (a) $P(X>500)$, (b) $P(200<X<1000)$.

steps.explanation: **Spot:** lifetime, exponential. **Read off** $\lambda$ from the mean.
(b) **Rewrite** as a difference of tails, then **plug in**.

blocks.title: Example 9 · Exponential, memoryless · Tutorial 4 Q3
blocks.prompt: A TV tube’s lifetime (years) is exponential with $\lambda=0.1$. The tube is already 10 years old. What’s the chance it lasts another 10?

steps.explanation: **Plug in:** the old tube is as good as new, so it’s just a new tube lasting 10 years.

blocks.text: Extras: Gaussian and mixed
Gaussian (normal)
“Normal with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$”, written $X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$. $\mu$ = the centre of the bell, $\sigma$ = how wide it is, $\sigma^2$ = the variance.
You can’t integrate the bell curve by hand. So **standardise**: $z$ = how many $\sigma$’s you are from the centre. Then read $\Phi(z)=P(Z\le z)$ from the table.
Topic 1’s rules, with $\Phi$ in place of $F$:
For a range centred on $\mu$ (within $k$ standard deviations), both tails are the same size:
**Backwards** (given a probability, find $x$): find the $z$ whose $\Phi(z)$ is the chance **below** $x$, then undo the standardising:
**Variance or standard deviation?** “$\sigma^2=2.25$” means $\sigma=1.5$. Dividing by $2.25$ is the most common lost mark.

blocks.title: Example 10 · Gaussian, forwards · Lecture 11
blocks.prompt: A sensor’s error $X$ is normal with $\mu=0$ and $\sigma=0.5$. What’s the chance $|X|<0.8$?

blocks.title: Example 11 · Gaussian, backwards · Tutorial 4 Q4
blocks.prompt: Test scores are $N(500,100^2)$. Which score marks the top $10\%$?

blocks.title: Example 12 · Gaussian, two cut-offs · Practice 03 Q8
blocks.prompt: Diastolic blood pressure is normal with $\mu=80$, $\sigma=7$ (mm Hg). $\ge95$ is hypertensive; strictly between $89$ and $95$ is mild hypertension. What percent of people are in each group?

steps.explanation: **Standardise** both cut-offs (2 decimals, like the table).

blocks.text: Mixed: a jump and a ramp
“With probability $q$ it is **exactly** $x_0$, otherwise it’s spread over a range.” That’s a mixed $X$: part discrete, part continuous.

items: **Jump:** an exact value with real chance. On the CDF it’s a jump, and the jump size is the chance: $P(X=x_0)=q$.
**Spread:** the rest of the time, $X$ has its usual PDF, but it only gets the **leftover** chance $1-q$. So multiply that PDF by $1-q$.
**Any probability** = the jumps inside the range + the area over the range.

blocks.text:
**Discrete = all jumps, continuous = all slope, mixed = both.**

blocks.title: Example 13 · Mixed: build the CDF · Lectures 10–11
blocks.prompt: A received signal is lost ($X=0$) with probability $0.2$. Otherwise its level is uniform on $(0,10)$. Find the CDF and $P(2<X<5)$.

steps.explanation: **Spread:** the uniform PDF times the leftover $0.8$.
**Accumulate:** the jump first, then the ramp.
**Rewrite** $P(2<X<5)$: the jump at $0$ isn’t inside, so only area counts.

blocks.title: Example 14 · Mixed: daily rainfall
blocks.prompt: On a given day it doesn’t rain with probability $0.6$ ($X=0$). If it rains, the amount $X$ (mm) is exponential with $\lambda=0.5$. (a) Find the CDF of $X$. (b) Find $P(X>2)$. (c) Find $P(X\le1)$.

steps.explanation: **Spot:** an exact value ($0$) with chance $0.6$, plus a spread → mixed.
(a) **Jump** of $0.6$ at $0$, then the exponential CDF scaled by $0.4$.
(b) **Rewrite:** only rainy days can go above 2. The exponential tail times $0.4$.

blocks.text: Practice Questions

**Question 2 is always these, in parts (a), (b), (c):**

1. **PDF ↔ CDF ↔ probability:** find $c$ (total area $=1$), integrate for $F$, differentiate for $f$, probabilities $=F(b)-F(a)$.
2. **Uniform:** length ÷ total length. **Exponential:** $P(X>x)=e^{-\lambda x}$; “already lasted” → memoryless.
3. **Gaussian:** $z=\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ → $\Phi$ table; $\Phi(-z)=1-\Phi(z)$; backwards $x=\mu+z\sigma$.
4. **Mixed:** jump = exact chance; spread × $(1-q)$; add jumps + area.
Test-style, easy → hard. Solve on paper first, then open the solution.

blocks.title: Question 1 · Uniform · Tutorial 4 Q5
blocks.prompt: Flights leave every half hour (9:00, 9:30, 10:00, …). A passenger arrives at a uniform random time between 8:45 and 9:45 A.M. Find the probability the passenger waits (a) **at most 10 minutes**, (b) **at least 15 minutes**.

steps.explanation: **Type:** uniform. $T$ = minutes after 8:45, total length $60$. Flights leave at $T=15,\ 45,\ 75$.
(a) **Rewrite:** wait $\le10$ means arriving in the 10 minutes before a flight.
(b) **Rewrite:** wait $\ge15$ means the next flight is 15+ minutes away.

blocks.title: Question 2 · Exponential, memoryless · like Lecture 10
blocks.prompt: The length $X$ (minutes) of a phone call is exponential with $\lambda=0.25$. Find (a) $P(X>4)$, (b) $P(2<X<6)$, (c) the chance a call that has already lasted 3 minutes lasts **more than 7** in total, (d) the time $t$ with $P(X>t)=\tfrac12$.

blocks.title: Question 3 · PDF ↔ CDF · CDF → probabilities and PDF · Practice 02 Q4
blocks.prompt:
The Rayleigh random variable $R$ has CDF

$$
F_R(r)=\begin{cases}0,&r<0\\ 1-e^{-r^2/(2\sigma^2)},&r\ge0\end{cases}
$$

(a) Find $P(\sigma\le R\le2\sigma)$ and $P(R>3\sigma)$. (b) Find the PDF of $R$.

steps.explanation: **Type:** a CDF is given → PDF ↔ CDF (have $F$).
(a) **Rewrite** as a difference. $\sigma$ cancels in each power.

blocks.title: Question 4 · PDF ↔ CDF · find $c$, then the CDF · Tutorial 5 Q5
blocks.prompt: $X$ has PDF $f_X(x)=Cx^2$ for $|x|\le1$, and $0$ otherwise. (a) Find $C$. (b) Find the CDF. (c) Find $P(X>\tfrac12)$ and $P(|X|<\tfrac12)$.

steps.explanation: **Rewrite** as a difference. Small, because the PDF is near $0$ around $x=0$.

blocks.title: Question 5 · PDF ↔ CDF · find $c$ by parts · Tutorial 4 Q1
blocks.prompt: The time $X$ (minutes) between seeing two runners has PDF $f(x)=\lambda x e^{-x}$ for $x>0$. (a) Find $\lambda$. (b) Find the CDF. (c) Find the probability the next runner is seen in 2 to 5 minutes, and in at least 7 minutes.

blocks.title: Question 6 · PDF ↔ CDF · a triangle, then work backwards · Practice 02 Q2
blocks.prompt: $X$ has a triangle PDF: $0$ at $x=-a$, peak height $c$ at $x=0$, back to $0$ at $x=a$. (a) Find $c$ and $f_X(x)$. (b) Find the CDF. (c) Find $b$ with $P(|X|<b)=\tfrac12$.

steps.explanation: (a) **Type:** unknown height → total area $=1$. **Find $c$** with the triangle shortcut: base $2a$, height $c$.
The two sides are straight lines down from the peak.
(b) **Accumulate:** left half = a small triangle; right half = $1$ minus the small triangle still to come.

blocks.title: Question 7 · Gaussian · Tutorial 6 Q5
blocks.prompt: A rover’s distance travelled is $X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$ with $\mu=500$ m and $\sigma^2=2.25$ m². Find (a) $P(X<500)$, (b) $P(X=501)$, (c) $P(X>501)$ and $P(X>505)$.

steps.explanation: **Type:** normal. **Spot:** that’s the variance, so take the root.
(a) $500$ is the centre: half the bell is below it.

blocks.title: Question 8 · Gaussian, backwards · like Tutorial 4 Q4
blocks.prompt: Resistances are normal with $\mu=100\ \Omega$ and variance $4\ \Omega^2$. (a) What fraction are within $100\pm3\ \Omega$? (b) Find $t$ so that $95\%$ are within $100\pm t$. (c) Which value is exceeded by only $5\%$?

blocks.title: Question 9 · Mixed · a CDF with two jumps
blocks.prompt:
A clipped sensor reading $X$ has CDF

$$
F_X(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<0\\ 0.25+\tfrac x2,&0\le x<1\\ 1,&x\ge1\end{cases}
$$

(a) Why is $X$ mixed? (b) Find $P(X=0)$ and $P(X=1)$. (c) Find $P(0<X<1)$ and $P(X\le0.5)$. (d) Find the PDF of the spread part.

steps.explanation: (a) **Type:** $F$ jumps (exact values with real chance) **and** ramps → mixed.
(b) **Jump** sizes. At $1$, $F$ goes from $0.25+0.5=0.75$ up to $1$.
(c) **Rewrite:** only the ramp is strictly inside $(0,1)$.

blocks.title: Question 10 · Mixed · Practice 02 Q3
blocks.prompt:
$X$ has CDF

$$
F_X(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<-1\\ \tfrac13+\tfrac23(x+1)^2,&-1\le x\le0\\ 1,&x>0\end{cases}
$$

Find the probabilities of $A=\{X>\tfrac13\}$, $B=\{|X|\ge1\}$, $C=\{|X-\tfrac13|<1\}$, $D=\{X<0\}$.

steps.explanation: **Type:** $F$ jumps from $0$ to $\tfrac13$ at $x=-1$, then rises smoothly → mixed.
$A$: **Rewrite** as one minus. $X$ is never above $0$.
